paragraphs: He is mentioned in Gittin, chapter 4, halakhah 2, where he spoke to Rabbi Yudan Nesia. Hyman says it seems the reading should be R' Oshaya Rabbah.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The suggested Oshaya Rabbah reading remains Hyman’s tentative emendation.

The whole Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:2 paragraph fully names Rabbi Oshaya bar Abba speaking TO Rabbi Yudan Nesia. Those local full titles are supported. Hyman’s it-seems/should-read Oshaya Rabbah proposal remains tentative; that uncollated alternative title is R'. The current mixed note stays verbatim and neither the patronymic nor the proposed identity is harmonized.
